target.name: Orangewood Labs
target.founder: Abhinav Das, Aditya Bhatia, Akash Bansal

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $5M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $1.8B.

data.narrative:
Orangewood Labs is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $5M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 9 private and 1 public firm in the robotics sector, including peers at similar and adjacent stages: Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B, Seed).

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $5M total raised as a base proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, implies a $10M valuation. Peer-median analysis across the three identified comparables yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.1B to $1.8B. The peer cohort spans seed through Series B stages, providing context for both earlier and later-stage positioning.

Triangulation of these two methods produces a range of $8M to $1.9B, with a median of $830M. The wide dispersion reflects methodological divergence: stage-progression anchors to current capital deployed, while peer-median reflects valuations of more mature, downstream-stage firms. Key uncertainties include whether the peer set—predominantly Series B companies—appropriately reflects Series A risk and execution progress, and whether Orangewood's technology trajectory and market traction support positioning toward the upper or lower end of observed peer multiples.
